title: n-core nonemptiness = NVM minor vanishing = list-decoding-beyond-Johnson shape: F17/F4/F15 collapse onto n-not-divides-a
evidence: Reproduced the in-tree linear-algebra dichotomy exactly at PROPER-subgroup prize-regime primes (mu_n dyadic, n=8/16/32, p=1 mod n, p~n^4, m=(p-1)/n>1) with exact mod-p Bareiss determinants. (1) det(zeta^(beta_j*i))_{Fin n x Fin n} != 0 <=> beta distinct mod n <=> n-core empty; for rectangle a^h (0<h<n) this is exactly n|a -- matches HOMDSSmoothObstruction.homds_det_ne_zero_iff_nCoreEmpty and RectNCore.rectBeta_nCoreEmpty_iff (both in ArkLib.lean build graph, axiom-clean per their #print axioms). So the F17 linear-algebra half is genuinely PROVEN. BUT the connection's substantive identification F17=F4 (minor-vanishing = list large beyond Johnson) is REFUTED as an equivalence by three exact facts: FACT1 k-independence -- the in-tree object is the FULL n x n Vandermonde; its verdict (n|a) has zero dependence on code dimension k or decoding radius e, while beyond-Johnson reachability flips across k at FIXED minor verdict (probe: a=n+1, n|/a so minor=0 for all h,k; beyond-Johnson reachable toggles True->False as k sweeps 2..n-1). FACT2 the minor is non-zero only on the sparse multiples of n (3/31, 3/63, 3/127 of widths for n=8/16/32), carrying ~1/n of one bit -- it cannot discriminate list-large from list-small. (C) DIRECT decoupling: a planted received word with genuine RS list size 3 (>1) at radius beyond Johnson (n=8,p=521,k=2,e=5>Johnson 4) coexists with the minor toggling purely on width arithmetic (a=8 n|a -> minor!=0 ; a=2 n|/a -> minor=0), independent of the list size. Probes: scripts/probes/_407_conn/_C001_ncore_reachability.py, _C001_decouple.py, _C001_listdecode_correspondence.py.
reduced_to: The PROVEN content is only: det(zeta^(beta_j*i)) on the FULL smooth domain mu_n vanishes <=> the n beta-residues collide mod n (the degree-collapse map d |-> d mod n), and for rectangles that is n|a. This is a k- and radius-free DIVISIBILITY detector, decoupled from the actual list-decoding object. The genuine open content (F4 beyond-Johnson list size on non-multiple-of-n widths) is exactly the part this minor does NOT see. Sharper open statement: does any (k+1)x(k+1) GM-MDS SUBMINOR of RS[mu_n,k] -- the object that actually depends on k and the radius -- vanish on a REACHABLE adversarial agreement pattern in the window (1-sqrt rho, 1-rho)? That submatrix question, not the full n x n Vandermonde, is the real F4/F17 link, and it remains open.
wall: W-genericity: the in-tree minor is the degree-collapse d |-> d mod n taken at the WRONG (full mu_n / n x n) quotient -- the same mis-quotient flagged for LovettUnionDegreesInjective (cf C016). The k-dependent beyond-Johnson list size welds back to the standard explicit-RS list-decoding-beyond-Johnson open core (BCHKS Thm 1.9 / ABF26 prize wall).
honest_note: The two in-tree Lean theorems are real, axiom-clean, and correctly reproduced -- this is NOT a refutation of the Lean code. What is refuted is the EQUIVALENCE interpretation (F17 minor-silent <=> F4 list-large) advertised by the connection: the minor verdict is k- and radius-independent and non-trivial on only ~1/n of widths, so it cannot be equivalent to the k,e-dependent beyond-Johnson list-size property; planted beyond-Johnson lists decouple from it directly. The reachability question in the attack_plan was not affirmatively closed (no proof that window radius forces n|a, and no advance to the F4 lower bound); it is reframed as the genuinely open (k+1)-subminor question above. Probes are exact integer arithmetic at multiple proper-subgroup primes; the RS-list brute-force used small n=8 (interpolation over C(n,k) subsets) so the planted-list sizes are illustrative, not a tight beyond-Johnson list count. No closure claimed.
